entity: Groupon, Inc. — US employing entity (to confirm)
summary: No Texas or Dallas leave law: the Dallas sick-leave ordinance was struck down in 2021 and HB 2127 (Labor Code §1.005) bars cities from mandating leave. Paid time off is company policy, paid out on leaving only if the written policy promises it.

locationAssumption.citation: Texas Labor Code §1.005 (HB 2127, upheld by the Third Court of Appeals in July 2025): cities cannot regulate employment leave; the Dallas Earned Paid Sick Time ordinance was permanently enjoined in 2021

rule.citation: Leave is taken in hours of the scheduled shift
rule.note: Federal and state law set no counting rule for company PTO.

source.citation: Groupon US company holiday calendar (no private-sector statutory holidays in Illinois)
source.note: Calendar is a placeholder (no public Groupon US holiday list exists); all dates match OPM federal holiday observance rules.

rule.citation: Company holidays are paid days off outside the leave banks (policy assumption)
No statutory vacation entitlement: paid time off is company policy. Groupon's own Dallas posting describes "flexible PTO"
rule.note: Modelled as flexible PTO with no statutory floor; the statutory minimum is zero.

rule.citation: Flexible PTO: no accrual, usage tracked, no balance limit (company policy)
Flexible PTO has no balance to carry
No Texas rule on sickness during leave; company policy
Texas Payday Law (Texas Workforce Commission): accrued leave is payable on separation only if a written policy or agreement promises it; vacation is not required by Texas law

extras.label: FMLA
extras.citation: FMLA 29 U.S.C. 2601 et seq.: up to 12 workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave (eligibility: 12 months and 1,250 hours)
